video_title: Lakers Q&A: LeBron's Next Contract, Austin Reaves' Market Value, Are LA's Picks More Valuable?

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' offseason strategy involves retaining core players and active trade market
quotes.excerpt: I think it's a fool's errand to try to predict the specific moves.
quotes.quote: I think it's a fool's errand to try to predict the specific moves. One move I will say I'm fairly confident in is that they will re-sign Austin Reaves. I don't know exactly what the number is going to be, but I think it will be north of 35 million. I expect them to retain Jaxson Hayes. I expect them to try to retain Rui Hachimura and Marcus Smart, depending on the numbers for each of those guys. And I expect them to try to retain LeBron James as well, but that will be a little bit more complicated with the negotiation element and just how he feels about what they are presenting. Outside of that, in terms of specific moves, I think they are going to be active on the trade market, and they are uniquely positioned to acquire players into their cap space.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers can re-sign Austin Reaves while still pursuing Jalen Duren
quotes.excerpt: Yes, they can keep Austin Reaves if they were to sign Jalen Duren.
quotes.quote: Yes, they can keep Austin Reaves if they were to sign Jalen Duren. I continue to say that Austin Reaves' contract situation is separate from the Lakers' cap space. Now, technically it relates to the cap space in the sense of if Austin walks, the Lakers would get an additional 21 million in cap space, but you are not replacing Austin Reaves with 21 million dollars. So, assuming that they keep him on the cap hold and re-sign him to some number above that, which again, I think is the way this is going to play out, that projected cap space that the Lakers would have to sign Jalen Duren or make an offer sheet for him would be separate from Austin.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' max contract value and its impact on Lakers' roster construction
quotes.excerpt: I think his max is a little high in terms of his cap hold is nearly 60 million dollars.
quotes.quote: I think his max is a little high in terms of his cap hold is nearly 60 million dollars, and if you were actually giving him the max, that would be over 60, which I think is too high in my regardless of the context of the Lakers' cap situation and how that would hamstring their ability to add to the roster. I think that number to me is too high. If you're talking even 40, 45 million, I think he was at that level overall for the season. I think it's probably fair. If you really wanted to argue up to 50, I would entertain that. I don't think I would go above that. The issue here is if the Lakers pay LeBron that much money, they are almost certainly going to either lose Marcus Smart and Rui Hachimura in pursuit of other players, or they are going to keep Marcus Smart and Rui Hachimura and have limited means to add to the roster.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Impact of 3-2-1 lottery system on the value of Lakers' future draft picks
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers' future firsts are now more valuable, and that was part of what I have in the show title.
quotes.quote: The Lakers' future firsts are now more valuable, and that was part of what I have in the show title. I don't know how much more valuable. I've seen some people say like they've doubled in value. I think that's a bit aggressive, but you could say they've increased by maybe 25%, 30% in value, which is a notable amount. And that to me makes so, I mean, maybe putting two firsts on the table is more equivalent to almost putting three firsts on the table, or, you know, two and a half, 2.6, 2.7, whatever, which you round up and it's closer to three. Maybe some of the conversations that the Lakers couldn't get in with their two future firsts are now conversations they can get in.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Building a team to beat the Oklahoma City Thunder's rotation
quotes.excerpt: I would pick Victor Wembanyama as my primary star.
quotes.quote: I would pick Victor Wembanyama as my primary star. This is some of the worst basketball we've just seen Shai Gilgeous-Alexander play, and I've got to give a lot of credit to Stephen Castle as the primary point of attack guy, iso guy, playing a lot of one-on-one against him. But Victor Wembanyama lurking has clearly affected Shai to some degree, and he's just a cheat code defensively. So, I would pick Victor Wembanyama as my primary star. I mean, if I could go Victor Wembanyama and Luka Doncic, like that's great, right? I don't I feel like that's cheating a little bit. So I I don't want to go with like two top five guys. That to me is so I I would pick Victor Wembanyama as my cheat code defensively against OKC. I mean, he's also disrupted Chet Holmgren. He's disrupted a lot of their stuff at the rim and in the paint.
